problem: Embodied chain-of-thought VLAs rely on rigid, one-size-fits-all reasoning templates (objects, plans, affordances, etc.) that make the policy process irrelevant information, and reasoning quality cannot be verified without an already-good policy (circular dependency).
motivation: Robotics has no internet-scale corpus linking vision and language to action, so which reasoning actually informs control is an unobserved latent variable. Indiscriminately using all web-derived reasoning primitives yields verbose, distracting traces and high latency, while manual annotation engineering is expensive.
key_idea: Treat embodied reasoning as a latent variable and use importance-weighted variational inference (a jointly trained prior/posterior VLA plus sampling-importance-resampling) to select reasoning traces that are predictive of expert actions, then retrain the VLA on those refined traces.
insight: Importance weights p(Z,A|C)/q(Z|C,A) estimate the information benefit of a reasoning strategy, so action-informative primitives are amplified and distracting ones suppressed without external rewards. Ablations show that refining only the Visible Objects primitive raises SR to 80.3% (vs 76.1% listing all objects) and raises the object criticality rate from 0.03% to 25.02%. An injected useless 'weather' primitive is pruned more aggressively than the others, and collision rate falls with more posterior samples K, saturating around K=16.
method: Reasoning primitives: Hypothesize a set of primitives (plan, visible objects, subtask, move, gripper position, affordances, etc.) whose text is generated by foundation models, the VLM itself, or human annotations.
Reasoning dropout warmstart: For each demo, build M traces by independently dropping each primitive with probability d, giving a diverse set of strategies from concise to verbose.
Joint prior/posterior training: One VLA is trained with half the data as the prior p(Z,A|C) (context -> reasoning -> action) and half as the posterior q(Z|C,A) (context + action -> reasoning).

Refine via SIR: Sample K candidates from the posterior, compute w=p(Z,A|C)/q(Z|C,A) from model log-probs, and resample one trace from Cat(w) per demo. Proposition: the log-ratio of expected weights equals the information benefit.
Bootstrap: Retrain the final VLA from base initialization on the refined dataset {(Z*,A|C)}; dropout means it can also run with reasoning suppressed ('Action Forcing') at test time.
Inference infrastructure: Extended SGLang-VLA for high-throughput repeated sampling and log-prob extraction for Prismatic-style VLAs.

setting.backbone: MiniVLA 1B (LIBERO-90), OpenVLA 7B (Bridge/WidowX), Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B MoE (NaviTrace), Qwen3-VL-4B (nuScenes); all fine-tuned
setting.training_data: LIBERO-90 demos, Bridgev2, NaviTrace (~1000 tasks, 500 scenes), and nuScenes, each with synthetic reasoning primitives (Llama 2/Molmo, Gemini 1.0, Qwen3-VL self-generated, or human-annotated); warmstart M=4-32 traces per demo
setting.observation: monocular RGB image (front camera for driving) + language task
setting.action_space: discrete action tokens (VQ-VAE chunk tokens for LIBERO, 7 tokens for Bridge), 2D image waypoints (NaviTrace), text-encoded 3 s ego trajectory (nuScenes)
setting.simulator: LIBERO-90; NaviTrace dataset (offline); nuScenes open-loop; WidowX real hardware
setting.privileged: Ground-truth expert actions are used for the posterior at training time only (plus GT waypoint path overlaid when generating NaviTrace reasoning); none at test time

numbers.extra: 20 rollouts per task; avg generated tokens 129.3 vs 256.8 for all primitives

numbers_note: Navigation per-embodiment scores and the K-scaling and dropout ablations are only in figures. No R2R-style VLN benchmark is reported. Hardware results are per-task only.
results: R&B-EnCoRe beats the all-primitives baseline on LIBERO-90 (79.5% vs 78.6%, no reasoning 75.9%) with about half the tokens. On real WidowX it is more robust OOD and faster (about 3 s vs over 5 s per step). It improves NaviTrace cumulative score from 19.6 to 39.4 and nuScenes avg collision rate from 0.38 to 0.30 (avg L2 0.73 to 0.68).
limitations: Requires training an additional prior/posterior warmstart model, which may be computationally prohibitive for larger models

Effectiveness depends on the diversity and coverage of the hypothesized primitives, and the gains on LIBERO-90 are modest; some evaluations are small (13 trials per hardware task) and the nuScenes evaluation is open-loop
The information-benefit proposition assumes the prior and posterior converge to the dropout-induced data distribution
